findings.issue: Fail-closed hole at the version/missing-row boundary (spec AC-4/AC-12, NF-3; ADR §4.2). maskFields treats a field as 'classified' ONLY if a classification row exists for (resourceType, facetField, facetSchemaVersion). When the handle facet's schema version has NO rows at all (or a field that SHOULD be classified has no row for its version), every field falls into the `cls === undefined` branch and is returned RAW (line 367-370). The build's own test documents this: ctx([],'public') over RAW returns all three fields raw (test line 234-237, comment: 'classified fields fall through as unclassified (kept raw)'). The spec AC-4 demands the opposite: 'a classified facet whose facet_schema_version has no matching data_classification rows yields MAXIMAL masking ... the field does not leak raw', and ADR §4.2 says 'facetSchemaVersion has no rows at all for that version ⇒ the whole classified facet is max-masked (NOT widened to whole-resource)'. The readFacetVersion doc-comment (line 191-193) explicitly CLAIMS this fail-closed policy 'lives in maskFields' — but maskFields does not implement it. Root cause is architectural: TypedFacet = {fields, schemaVersion} carries NO signal of WHICH fields are classified independent of row-presence, so 'genuinely unclassified field (raw is correct)' is indistinguishable from 'classified field whose rows are missing (must fail-closed)'. The v2-mismatch test (line 240-249) only drops ssn because clearance is null, NOT because of the version mechanism — the version-boundary fail-closed AC is not actually exercised in isolation. Bounded blast radius: visibility is still capped by the grant facet upstream (visibleFields), so this cannot widen beyond grant-conferred fields; but on a security-узел the red-line is 'doubt resolves to zero visibility', and a value-suppressing AC that the code inverts is a spec-vs-code divergence, not a nit.
findings.suggestion: Architect-level: give the model a way to know a field is classified-in-this-facet independent of a present row — e.g. a per-(resourceType, schemaVersion) 'declared classified field set' from the ClassificationSource, so a declared-classified field with NO row for its version fails closed to drop/redact instead of falling through raw; OR have TypedFacet/handle declare which fields are classified. Then add a fitness test that isolates the version-boundary (rows exist for version N, handle is version M≠N, NON-null clearance ⇒ classified field max-masked, raw never present) — the current FF-DC4/DC12 test leans on null clearance and does not prove the version mechanism. Until then the readFacetVersion doc-comment overstates the implemented guarantee.

deviations_assessment.ref: deriveClearance reads grant.constraint FIRST, grant.resourceFacet as fallback (ADR §4.3 said resourceFacet OR constraint)
deviations_assessment.verdict: legitimate (arguably a correctness improvement over the ADR's loose 'OR')
deviations_assessment.rationale: A whole-resource grant MUST keep resourceFacet strictly absent — that is the ONLY widen path (grant-resolver.test.ts:450-460; a present-but-malformed resourceFacet fails closed to zero fields per R-1). If clearance had to ride on resourceFacet, a whole-resource grant could never carry clearance (placing {clearance} there would make resourceFacet present-malformed ⇒ zero fields). constraint-first is therefore NECESSARY for whole-resource + clearance-bearing grants, which FF-DC7 (grant-resolver.test.ts:596-621) explicitly exercises. Grant semantics not broken: a whole-resource grant without resourceFacet correctly reads clearance from constraint; a no-clearance whole-resource grant over a classified field correctly drops it (test line 662-676, fail-closed).

role_gap_evidence: Security-узел review surfaced an architectural fail-closed gap (R-1) that the build's own fitness test documents in a comment yet does not catch as red — the FF-DC4/DC12 test leans on null clearance and never isolates the version-boundary mechanism, so a green gate masked a security-AC inversion. Candidate evidence for ledgers/role-gaps.md: fitness checks for fail-closed ACs should be required to isolate the failing mechanism (here: version mismatch with NON-null clearance), not satisfy the assertion via an adjacent lever (null clearance).
